title: Certify an exact 280-row P112 demand kernel (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped equivalence proof with an exact finite certificate, produced by Nick Petalas. For the 14-rectangle alphabet obtained by uniting Jeremy Diviney's two PR1422 support layouts and the eight coordinate rectangles, all orthogonal-clique rank demands are equivalent to 280 saved rows for every nonnegative multiplicity vector.

```text
262,928 complete clique demands
  -> 1,141 equal-hit-signature maxima
  -> 280 pairwise nondominated witnessed inequalities
```

This answers PR1422 Open next question 2 for one specified alphabet. Every omitted row has an explicit retained dominator. The contribution is the smaller equivalent necessary-condition system, not a replay or audit of the predecessor's counts, costs or decoder result. I stopped at this first strict reduction.

Only `research/p112-demand-kernel/` is added. No new kappa, selected-frontier change, physical supplier or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. Credit Jeremy Diviney / PR1422 for the question, complete-clique guard and saved caps; Cinna Davis / PR1347 and PR1323 for the geometry and support model; Navinor, David Arias, Hanson Sun, DreamingOfClouds, themilkman216 and the retained E8/label/decoder lineage. Equal-row quotienting and monotone inequality dominance are classical. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Evidence

Before, the complete cap screen contains 262,928 inequalities, including demands not obtained from subsets of full frames. After, the generated 280-row kernel preserves precisely that complete screen for arbitrary nonnegative real multiplicities, including unbounded integer term counts. Each retained row has an original clique witness. Pairwise nondominance is not a minimum-family or linear-program irredundancy claim.

Local CPython 3.12.15 checks pass at head `092dcbd13d1263e691ad29f34fbf286fea1fac2c`:

- Registered metadata/pins and both complete warning-strict normal/optimized commands. Individually timed commands took 8.68 and 8.04 seconds, below their 300-second limits. These are local durations, not a speedup claim.
- Two complete clique enumerations, every original domination implication and retained witness, all 16,384 binary multiplicities, 256 integer vectors and 3,456 toy equivalence cases.
- Positive coordinate and known deficient-layout controls, eight coordinate omissions, six malformed-certificate/domain controls, and a combined-inequality control preventing an irredundancy overclaim.
- Committed-byte, regular-mode and source-history preflight; the official ten-file export and declared-input coverage check. A read-only Git-free optimized export replay passed with identical scientific stdout and unchanged files. Both actual input-byte corruptions and an altered saved demand were rejected.

Exact reproduction commands, from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-demand-kernel
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/p112-demand-kernel/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/p112-demand-kernel/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p112-demand-kernel --check-source-history
```

Other hosts may substitute their CPython 3.12 path. Expected marker: `PASS_P112_DEMAND_KERNEL`, with `complete_demands=262928`, `signature_rows=1141`, `kernel_rows=280`. Standard library only. The normal verifier compares the complete generated certificate and prints a receipt bound to all eight package-file hashes. The only external live inputs are the two exact pinned PR1422 JSON files. No predecessor executable is imported or replayed.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The equivalence concerns exactly the declared support caps and their nonnegative multiplicities. Independent whole-term transposes are covered. Changed caps, new rectangles or an actual trimmed-support screen require rebuilding the quotient. A support-screen pass supplies neither coefficients nor a decoder.

No minimum-family theorem, COPY floor, new runtime percentage, complete signed invoice or physical/native implementation is supplied. Source access, dirty restoration, stock, compiler closure, precision/tape and outer integration remain unrun. No selected cold replay, Lean or Docker suite was run. All five selected framework assumptions remain.

## Related open work

- #6430 accelerates PR1325's P112 plane-compatibility census for a different alphabet; it computes no orthogonal-clique demand-kernel size.
- #6424 refutes a quotient-direction edge bound in a different six-line rational decoder model; it computes no instance of this fixed P112 cap screen.
- #5088 uses a different two-star support dictionary; this kernel is specific to the PR1422 caps.
- #5064 searches changed masked completions and bases; no such coefficient search is performed here.
- #2832 studies broad decoder floors and batching reductions; necessary-screen equivalence proves no such floor.
- #3154 reduces the general P112 floor to conjectures; this finite cap alphabet settles none of them.
- #3074 studies P112-to-P120 padding; this fixed P112 demand kernel supplies no padding theorem.
- #3045 studies fitting matrices and root-code floors; this result has no fitting-matrix or coefficient claim.
- #3029 studies two-sided deficiency budgets; the present screen does not classify two-sided coefficients.
- #2985 studies one-sided residue closures; this result makes no new residue or COPY-floor claim.
- #3566 binds a tetrad decoder to selected ports; its support alphabet and physical obligations differ.
- #3604 studies tetrad fusion and consumer costs; no such invoice is evaluated here.
- #3916 audits dirty-input tetrad coefficients; this result supplies no coefficient or dirty-input audit.
- #3918 studies selected-centre demand floors; this result concerns orthogonal-clique cap inequalities.
- #4090 accelerates a deletion census; its domain and scientific quantity differ.
- #2375 accelerates frame-pair enumeration; this reduction retains all nonmaximal clique demands.

These contributions are cited at their own declared scopes. This result computes no competing COPY optimum or kappa value; no extra computation was run to audit their numbers.

Completion overlap checked all 14 account open PRs created since the advance claim, including this PR. The other 13 contain no competing value for this fixed-alphabet kernel; no shared-instance numerical disagreement was identified. No additional computation audited another contribution.

## Open next questions

1. Can nonnegative combinations remove a retained row? Start with one row and an exact rational Farkas certificate from the others. Such combined redundancy is uncomputed.
2. Can changed caps pass the complete screen below COPY64 and then admit exact coefficients? Specify the changed alphabet and rebuild the quotient first. Coefficient synthesis and a fully charged physical caller remain separate blockers.

## CI notes

[Hosted run 41536724626](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41536724626) passed both `plan` and `replay (research/p112-demand-kernel)` at exact head `092dcbd13d1263e691ad29f34fbf286fea1fac2c`. The completed checks were read once; run metadata confirms successful completion and the matching head. The replay ran the declared bounded package checks and confirmed committed inputs remained unchanged.

All registered checks also passed locally, with committed-byte/source-history and read-only export checks as recorded above. Hosted success certifies execution of the declared finite checks and bindings. It does not supply independent mathematical acceptance, formal-kernel review or the unrun physical/compiler/outer obligations.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated research package. Existing sources, selected frontier and predecessor credits are unchanged.
